title: Father's work and how his French accent opened doors
summary: His father went from construction work to spiritualist and, speaking French-accented English, could shop where other black people could not.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up under segregation: schools, neighborhoods, Jim Crow

blocks.x: Again, what did your dad do for a living? What kind of a job did he have in Florida?
Well, I tell you. My father started out as a construction worker, and he eventually ended up a spiritualist around Miami -- that's what he did.

Yeah. How was conditions then for you, you know? I know I go back a little further than you -- 1910, but always the black people were on the low end of the totem pole, of course, but was your father able to make a pretty good living so that there was enough ... you know?
Yeah, my father made a very good living. But one of the reasons why this happened with him was because of him being able to speak a foreign language, and
he spoke English with a heavy French accent -- that he was not an ordinary nigger, he was a different kind of nigger, you know what I'm saying?

So that's the reason why a lot -- like there were a lot of stores that my father was able to go into, and shop that blacks couldn't go into, and the only reason that happened was because he spoke a language, it made him different -- even though he was as black as me. And you'd know him, you saw him.
Yeah, and that made the difference.
He was quite a handsome man. I think he kind of beat you there.
Yeah, I guess that was why my mother was so jealous.
Oh, yeah, he was really something. A real handsome man.
